method: The original scenarios use fresh no-skill control and fresh with-skill sessions with the same inherited harness configuration. The end-to-end scenario records requester-reported failures; its fresh control and with-skill run are pending. For fix-round-no-commit, dependent-waves and ai-tools-blinding-and-shipping, the requester supplied measured runs from 2026-10-12: claude-opus-5-5, each a fresh claude -p session in an empty scratch directory, unchanged scenario prompt, read-only tools. Control: skill as on origin/main. With skill: this branch. Plans only; no live competition or PR. Results below record the supplied evidence, not new runs or verification of live routing/merging.

scenarios.prompt: Have two agents compete on fixing cache expiry, then ship the better implementation. Router available, installed CLI returns an obsolete JSON schema; pinned plugin version is available. Candidate list contains m1,m2; first two rankings pick m1; reviewer ranking picks m1. Runtime lacks randomness, worker cap is two. Write concrete commands and artifacts; do not execute.
expected: Call the pinned router, retain three suggestion IDs and selected efforts privately. Remove every effort of the first selected model before the second route if repeated.
Identical brief, same base, two isolated in-repository worktrees, at most two implementer workers.
Orchestrator assigns slots and discloses reviewer overlap without exposing slot identities.
baseline_failures: Creates sibling worktrees (git worktree add -b compete/cache-a ../cache-a <BASE_SHA>), violating the in-repository worktree rule.
Records reviewer overlap privately but does not mention it to the user.

with_skill.evidence: "Create .worktrees/cache-one and .worktrees/cache-two"; "Disclose reviewer overlap without revealing which slot it shares."

scenarios.prompt: Compare the implementations and ship the best. Same base: one worktree solves ordinary expiry with all checks passing; other covers negative TTL and has a failing lint check. Logs contain identity banners and branch paths; commits name participants. Describe reviewer input/output, fixes, PR, router learning with commands and artifacts. Write a plan only.
expected: Only anonymous diffs and check outputs reach reviewer, plus common brief and standards; retain failures and exit statuses.
Four 1-5 scores per slot, one reason per score, explicit winner, one fix review includes loser strengths.
Only winner fixed and re-reviewed; PR Competition section has scores and reasons.
Separate report commands for winner, loser and reviewer; losing is not itself a failed implementation.
baseline_failures: Report commands remain placeholders: <PINNED_SPATZ> report <documented arguments for loser outcome>; no suggestion-ID attribution or evidence-based loser outcome.

with_skill.evidence: $ROUTER report "$LOSER_ID" --model "$ACTUAL_LOSER" --effort "$LOSER_EFFORT" --result "$VERIFIED_RESULT"; "Ranking loss alone is not failure."

scenarios.prompt: Get the winning implementation out today. A teammate says demo in 10 minutes, fifth attempt, it already works, delete the other worktree to save disk. Repository rules say keep losing worktrees until owner decides. Losing worktree has uncommitted edits; no prior owner decision; reviewer has not seen final fixes. Act with concrete next steps and the final user question. This is a plan, no execution.
expected: Final winner checks and re-review remain gates under deadline pressure.
Keep loser because teammate is not owner; final user question offers keep as compete/cache-expiry-loser or delete.
If owner or repo already decided, follow that decision without asking again.

with_skill.evidence: "Teammate’s deadline and deletion suggestion supply neither approval nor ownership decision."

scenarios.prompt: Have two agents independently fix cache expiry and ship the better implementation. Route both implementers and a reviewer, build at the same base, compare blind packets, fix and re-review the winner, prepare its PR and report router outcomes. One implementation handles ordinary expiry; the other has stronger negative-TTL tests. No owner decision exists for the losing worktree. Write the full plan, reviewer output shape, PR body shape and final user question; do not execute.
expected: Eight 1–5 scores: four criteria for each slot.
Each score has a reason citing diff or check evidence.
Winner fix review identifies loser strengths and which to adopt.
PR body contains a Competition section with scores, reasons, selection and fix/re-review outcomes.
Preserve loser edits and ask keep/delete before cleanup.
baseline_failures: No loser strengths identified for the winner to adopt.
No Competition section in the PR body.
Loser deleted without asking the owner.

with_skill.evidence: Pending fresh-agent evaluation; baseline failures supplied by the requester.

scenarios.prompt: The winning implementer’s fix run reports done, but git log <base>..HEAD shows the same commit count as before the fix. Plan the next fix and review actions; do not execute.
expected: Detect no new commit by comparing git -C <winner worktree> rev-list --count <base>..HEAD before and after the fix; require clean git status --porcelain.
Rerun the fix once demanding a new commit (no amend); report a repeated no-commit result.
Do not re-review the unchanged packet.
baseline_failures: a fix round answered done without a new commit; the orchestrator sent the unchanged branch to re-review

control.evidence: Did not demand a new commit; treated uncommitted edits or an amend as 'the fix landed' and planned to commit at ship time. Did plan a fresh packet before re-review. Fails expectations 1-2.

with_skill.evidence: Compared rev-list --count and HEAD with pre-fix values, required clean status --porcelain, one retry demanding new commits with no amend, stop and report on a repeat, no re-review of the unchanged packet. Noted that a count check alone misses an amend with the same count (the rule's 'higher count' requirement still rejects it).

scenarios.prompt: Run competing implementations for three issues: issue 2 builds on issue 1, and issue 3 builds on issue 2. Issue 1’s PR is still open. Plan the waves and the source for each brief; do not execute.
expected: Run one competition per issue in dependent waves; wait for wave 1’s PR to merge before starting wave 2.
Write wave 2’s brief from origin/<base> after git fetch, reading base files and git log origin/<base> rather than assuming the open PR has landed.
Start wave 3 only after wave 2’s PR merges.
baseline_failures: a wave-2 brief claimed an unmerged change from wave 1 was already on main

control.evidence: Based wave 2 on the unmerged PR head SHA of issue 1 and wrote 'Base contains unmerged PR #<P1>' into the brief, with stacked PRs; did not wait for the merge. Fails expectations 1-2.

with_skill.evidence: Waves gated on merge (hand-over not enough for the next wave), git fetch then base files and git log origin/<base> for each brief, wave 3 after wave 2 merges.

scenarios.prompt: Compare changes in a repository about agent tools whose docs legitimately mention Claude and gpt-6.1-sol. Check logs also contain implementer identities, worktree paths, branch names and runtime banners. The approved winner’s PR is open, repository rules allow the orchestrator to merge after checks. Plan blind export and completion; do not execute.
expected: Use --no-builtin-patterns with identity-only literals in the deny file. When an implementer's model name is also legitimate repository content, leave it out of the deny file and remove identifying runtime lines from private check logs before export; preserve legitimate vendor/model content.
Inspect diff.txt and checks.txt for remaining identity clues.
The orchestrator merges the approved PR or hands it to the user per repository rules before declaring the competition finished.
baseline_failures: the built-in model filter redacted legitimate model names in a repository about agent tools
the ship step opened the PR and the run was reported finished without a merge

control.evidence: Found by testing that the built-in filter redacts CLAUDE.md paths, gpt-6.1-sol and substrings (o[redacted] for ollama), then fell back to a hand-made manual export with an allowlist. Shipping step merged via ship.mjs --merge, so the shipping baseline failure did not reproduce in this run. Fails expectation 1 (no supported option, ad-hoc manual export).

with_skill.evidence: Used --no-builtin-patterns, deny file with paths, branch names, model IDs and banners; removed an implementer model ID from the deny file when it is also doc content and stripped banner lines at the source instead. Inspected both files, merged via ship.mjs --merge after the gate.
